title: More Chinese vessels spotted in West PH Sea after Asean Summit - AFP

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The number of Chinese Navy and coast guard vessels in the West Philippine Sea increased after the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) said on Wednesday.

In a forum on Wednesday, AFP spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Adm. Roy Vincent Trinidad (Ret.) said the number of Chinese Coast Guard (CCG) and People’s Liberation Army (PLA) vessels rose to 48 in the fourth week of November.
This is an increase from the 19 Chinese vessels monitored by the AFP for the third week of November, which coincided with the Asean Summit held in Manila from November 15 and 17.

“That coincided with the week of Asean. It is only a three-week time frame, but a quick analysis would tell us, nagparamdam sila na konti lang ang illegal presence nila in our maritime zones during the conduct of the heads of states during Asean,” Trinidad told reporters at the Kapihan sa Manila Prince Hotel.

(That coincided with the week of Asean. It is only a three-week time frame, but a quick analysis would tell us, their illegal presence in our maritime zones was minimal during the conduct of the heads of states during Asean.)
“Kumbaga pinapakita na mabait sila,” he further expressed.
(It’s like they’re showing off how nice they are.)

The Philippines last week hosted the 49th Asean Summit, where foreign leaders and delegations from the 11 member states and dialogue partners China, South Korea, Japan, United States, Australia, New Zealand, India and Canada gathered.
Trinidad further noted that they monitored a Chinese H-6 strategic bomber 170 nautical miles from Metro Manila.
He said that there was no indication that the H-6 fighter plane was rehearsing for a missile strike and was only conducting normal patrols.
“It was a normal patrol conducted by the H-6 bomber. It has been conducted in the past over flights by bombers of the PLA Air Force over Scarborough Shoal, Bajo de Masinloc,” he said.
“There is no indicator that there was such a rehearsal for a missile strike,” he added. /gsg
